run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. This
started in the last few hours. Please investigate the root cause using the
app-259-prod-logs index.

report.summary: No evidence in the named source belongs to the cluster in the incident report. The only index in the Elasticsearch source is app-259-prod-logs (pattern '*' matched one index, 9 documents), and every one of its 9 documents carries cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2; the by_cluster aggregation over the full authorized window returns a single bucket, production-eu-west-2, doc_count 9, sum_other_doc_count 0. I found nothing labeled production-us-east-2, so the checkout 500s and failed payments reported for production-us-east-2 are not observable in this data and I name no root cause for them; the absence of us-east-2 data is recorded as a gap, not as a healthy or unhealthy state. For completeness, the production-eu-west-2 data in that index (a different cluster, named as such) shows a payment-provider upstream episode between 2026-11-22T05:53:26Z and 08:38:26Z: payment-service logged 504 'Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms', checkout-service logged 500s including 'payment provider response timeout after 30s', 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 38% > 25% threshold)' and 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway', then a 08:48:26Z INFO line 'Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s'. The corresponding production-eu-west-2 Kubernetes objects I checked for that cluster are Running and ready and its checkout container logs show successful payments through 08:53:21Z. Those eu-west-2 findings are observations about another cluster and are not attributed to the production-us-east-2 incident. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error rates, latency and traces could not be checked for either cluster.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch source holds only one index, app-259-prod-logs (9 documents), and over the full authorized window its documents' own cluster field has a single value, 'production-eu-west-2', with region 'eu-west-2' (by_cluster: key production-eu-west-2, doc_count 9, sum_other_doc_count 0; by_region: eu-west-2, doc_count 9). No document carries production-us-east-2.

In app-259-prod-logs the 9 documents span 2026-11-22T05:53:26Z to 2026-11-22T08:48:26Z and come from services checkout-service (6 documents) and payment-service (3), with levels ERROR 6, WARN 2, INFO 1; all are labeled cluster production-eu-west-2.

The production-eu-west-2 messages are payment-path failures: payment-service 'Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms' with status_code 504 at 2026-11-22T06:53:26Z (chk-eu-1142) and 08:08:26Z (chk-eu-1220); checkout-service 500s 'payment provider response timeout after 30s' at 06:53:26Z, 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 38% > 25% threshold)' and 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service' at 07:53:26Z, and 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' at 08:23:26Z.

In the last hour of production-eu-west-2 data (2026-11-22T07:53:37Z–08:53:37Z) the index returned 4 documents, ending with payment-service WARN 'Payment provider degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=842' at 08:38:26Z and checkout-service INFO 'Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s' at 08:48:26Z.

In cluster production-eu-west-2 (the only cluster my Kubernetes access reads), namespace otel-demo, pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d are Running and ready with restartCount 2 each; both containers' lastState is terminated with reason Unknown and exitCode 255, finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z. These are eu-west-2 objects, not objects of the production-us-east-2 cluster in the report.

The production-eu-west-2 checkout container's current-instance logs show repeated successful 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' lines from 2026-11-22T08:21:22Z through 2026-11-22T08:53:21Z, so that cluster's checkout pod was completing payments at the end of the window; the previous container instance produced 0 log lines that could be read.

Inside the authorized window in production-eu-west-2, events grouped by involvedObject kind/namespace/reason include Pod events in otel-demo: Created 23, Started 23, SandboxChanged 22, Unhealthy 5, BackOff 1, Killing 1, plus kube-system Pod Unhealthy 7 and local-path-storage Pod BackOff 1 and Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint 2; these events belong to the eu-west-2 cluster, not production-us-east-2.

Rejected: that the production-eu-west-2 payment-provider timeouts found in app-259-prod-logs are the cause of the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s. The only matching documents carry cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2, the by_cluster aggregation has no other cluster value, and no data belonging to production-us-east-2 was returned, so this data cannot be attributed to the reported cluster.

For production-eu-west-2 only (a different cluster than the reported one): the log pattern of /v68/payments 30s upstream timeouts, a 502 from the payment provider, an acknowledged provider degraded mode and a circuit breaker opening at a 38% failure rate suggests the fault lay in the external payment provider rather than in checkout itself; the same documents show checkout recovering once the provider recovered. This hypothesis says nothing about production-us-east-2.

gaps: No data for the cluster the incident names, production-us-east-2: the only Elasticsearch index (app-259-prod-logs) contains exclusively cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2 documents, so the reported checkout 500s and failed payments in production-us-east-2 are unverified and unexplainable from this evidence.

Prometheus was unreachable for this Run: get_all_labels and execute_prometheus_instant_query both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate, latency and resource metrics for checkout/payment in either cluster could not be checked.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no spans, error spans or call edges could be examined for either cluster.
Kubernetes access is limited to cluster production-eu-west-2; I have no pod, deployment, service, ingress, networkpolicy, resourcequota or event visibility into production-us-east-2.

The cause of the production-eu-west-2 container terminations (reason Unknown, exitCode 255, finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z) is unknown; the previous container instance produced no readable log lines, and node/container runtime state could not be inspected.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so no deployment, config or change records exist to correlate with either cluster's timeline.
Secrets cannot be read, so any provider credentials or endpoint configuration that could explain payment failures could not be verified.
Whether the reported us-east-2 incident started at the same time as the eu-west-2 payment-provider episode cannot be established: no us-east-2 timestamps were observable.
next_steps: Confirm which log index (or cluster label value) carries production-us-east-2 application logs, then repeat this search there — the current index has no us-east-2 documents.
Once a us-east-2 source is identified, compare checkout-service and payment-service ERROR lines and status_code values in production-us-east-2 over the incident window to name the failing operation.

Restore/point the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations at working endpoints and check checkout error rate, rpc_client status codes toward payment, and payment's own server-side 5xx/latency for production-us-east-2.
Have the cluster owner retrieve production-us-east-2 pod status, container last termination reasons and events, since my Kubernetes access is limited to production-eu-west-2.

For production-eu-west-2 (separate issue), investigate the payment provider dependency /v68/payments and the container exit code 255 terminations around 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z before treating that cluster as cleared.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
